own_solution.law: For an approaching source and a stationary listener in still air, f_heard = f_emitted c/(c-v_source) = 440(343)/(343-20).
assumptions: The stated source speed applies throughout the relevant emission.
The listener receives the steady tone before the source passes.
For the subsequent tuning sentence, the requested frequency is that received after the tuning change reaches the listener.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TEDCB and T62DC replace the specified 16 Hz adjustment with an unspecified 'small amount', so these variants do not preserve the same stated number and unit as required.

notes: The base physics is well-posed under the ordinary steady-reception interpretation. Initial distance enters the arrival-time relation t_arrival = t_emission + (d_initial - v_source t_emission)/c, but cancels when computing successive arrival intervals. TD410 is read as saying that the given 440 Hz was measured after the adjustment: (440 - 16) + 16 = 440 Hz. T8B99 instead raises the emitted frequency from 440 to 456 Hz. Earlier-run adjustments provide no additional input to the present run, whose initial emitted frequency is already specified. The unspecified adjustments do not prevent numerical solutions for their individual sentences because those sentences are disconnected; the defect concerns the required matching of variant quantities.
